title: The Book of Hours
significance: A cycle that borrows the form of a monk's prayer to address God not as a finished being but as one still being made. This is the collection that first made Rilke's name known in the German-speaking world.

title: New Poems
significance: A collection in which the method of the thing-poem — gazing at a single object, such as a panther, a rose, or an ancient sculpture, and building it into a poem — is realized at the scale of a full book. It is the result of translating Rodin's working method into a procedure for poetry.

title: The Notebooks of Malte Laurids Brigge
significance: A prose work that arranges the poverty and death of Paris and memories of childhood as a chain of short notations instead of a plot. It is an early instance of translating the experience of the modern city into a problem of novelistic form.

title: Duino Elegies
significance: A cycle of long poems begun in 1912 at Duino Castle and completed as ten elegies in 1922 at Muzot. The grammar of the late Rilke, which binds mourning and praise into a single idiom, is established here.

title: Sonnets to Orpheus
significance: A cycle of 55 sonnets written within a few days in February 1922. Within the strict frame of the fixed sonnet form, it treats song, death, and transformation, and it was completed in the same period as the Duino Elegies.

title: Letters to a Young Poet
significance: Ten letters written between 1903 and 1908 to the officer cadet Franz Xaver Kappus. It is a posthumous publication compiled by Kappus and published in 1929 after Rilke's death, and it is the most widely read of his prose writings on the attitude of writing poetry.

title: The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock
significance: A poem that overlays the internal monologue of a hesitant middle-aged speaker with an evening cityscape. Published in the Chicago magazine Poetry in 1915, it marked the point at which the idiom of English poetry changed.

title: The Sacred Wood: Essays on Poetry and Criticism
significance: His first collection of criticism, including Tradition and the Individual Talent. It presented a view of poetry as a rearrangement of tradition rather than an expression of the poet's personality, changing the direction of Anglo-American criticism.

title: The Waste Land
significance: A long poem that assembles the spiritual exhaustion of postwar Europe out of shifting speakers across five parts and quotations in several languages. It was heavily cut through Ezra Pound's editing to reach its present form.

title: Murder in the Cathedral
significance: A verse play on the martyrdom of Thomas Becket, first performed at the Canterbury Festival in 1935. It revived the chorus of Greek tragedy within English religious drama and opened Eliot's later career as a playwright.

title: Four Quartets
significance: A cycle that gathered into one volume in 1943 four long poems separately published between 1936 and 1942. It arranged questions of time, memory, and faith according to the structure of a musical movement.

title: Three Lives
significance: Three novellas, each treating the life of a different woman. It was in Melanctha especially that the method of narrating a character's consciousness through repeated constructions was first attempted.

title: Tender Buttons: Objects, Food, Rooms
significance: A collection of short prose poems organized under the headings of objects, food, and rooms. By stripping nouns of their referential function and arranging the words, it translated the problem of Cubism into language.

title: The Making of Americans
significance: A novel of more than 900 pages, written in the 1900s and published in Paris in 1925. It narrates a family's chronicle through typological classification and repeated constructions, halting the very progression of the narrative.

title: Composition as Explanation
significance: A lecture given at Oxford and Cambridge in 1926, published as a book the same year by the Hogarth Press. It is a primary source in which she explains, in her own words and using the term continuous present, how her prose handles time.

title: The Autobiography of Alice B. Toklas
significance: A memoir of herself written borrowing the first-person voice of her companion, Alice Toklas. It recorded figures of the Paris art world in anecdotes, achieved commercial success, and became the book that introduced Stein to a general readership.

title: In a German Pension
significance: Her first story collection, set in a boarding house at a Bavarian spa. Consisting of satirical sketches aimed at the German middle class, it shows the early method she would later abandon.

title: Prelude
significance: A novella that divides several days in which a New Zealand family moves house into a series of short scenes. It was hand-printed in 1918 by the Woolfs' Hogarth Press, and it is the work in which her method of shifting only point of view, without plot, became established.

title: Bliss and Other Stories
significance: A story collection containing the title story, Bliss, along with Prelude. It repeatedly attempts a structure in which the story ends the moment a character becomes aware of the condition of their own life.

title: The Garden Party and Other Stories
significance: The last story collection published in her lifetime. It contains the title story and At the Bay, and it is here that her method of treating class boundaries and death as a single moment of a character's shifting perception is at its clearest.

title: The Late Mattia Pascal
significance: The story of a man declared dead in an accident who tries and fails to live again under a new name. It is his first major work, an experiment in what remains once legal identity has disappeared.

title: On Humor
significance: A theoretical work analyzing the moment at which laughter flips into its opposite feeling. It is the text in which the author himself formulated the principle by which his novels and plays operate.

title: Six Characters in Search of an Author
significance: Six unfinished characters burst in on a theater company in rehearsal and demand that their story be written. Its 1921 Rome premiere ended in an uproar, but it went on to become the starting point of metatheater.

title: Henry IV
significance: A man who came to believe, after a fall from a horse, that he was a medieval emperor continues to play the role of a madman even after regaining his sanity. It is a play that compresses the problem of mask and identity into a single character's choice.

title: One, No One and One Hundred Thousand
significance: The record of a man who, starting from a single remark by his wife that his nose is crooked, goes on to dismantle his own identity to the very end. It is his last novel, a long-worked manuscript he completed by serializing it in 1925–26.

title: The Threepenny Opera
significance: A work that transposes John Gay's eighteenth-century ballad opera into Berlin's criminal underworld, set to music by Kurt Weill. Through a structure in which songs continually interrupt the plot, it established the devices of epic theater in popular form.

title: Svendborg Poems
significance: A poetry collection compiled in his Danish exile and published in Copenhagen in 1939. It handles the political statements of an exile in short, dry constructions, showing that the same method as his plays also works in poetry, and it was the last collection of new poems he published in his lifetime.

title: Mother Courage and Her Children
significance: A chronicle of a camp trader in the Thirty Years' War who loses all three of her children while trying to protect her trade. It was written in 1939 during his exile in Sweden and premiered in Zurich in 1941, and it was designed so that the audience sympathizes with the protagonist while not agreeing with her choices.

title: Life of Galileo
significance: It portrays Galileo, who recanted heliocentrism, as neither hero nor traitor but a calculating figure. He wrote the first draft in Denmark in 1938 and it premiered in Zurich in 1943, and he later rewrote it twice more, as an American version and a Berlin version.

title: The Good Woman of Setzuan
significance: The story of a woman who must play a ruthless cousin in order to survive as a good person, presenting as a stage experiment the question of whether goodness can coexist with economic conditions. It premiered in Zurich in 1943.

title: The Caucasian Chalk Circle
significance: A frame play that asks whether an abandoned child belongs to the servant who raised her or the noble mother who bore her. He wrote it in 1944 during his American exile, and it premiered first in English in the United States in 1948, with the German-language premiere following in 1954 on the Berliner Ensemble stage.

title: A Young Doctor's Notebook
significance: A cycle of stories based on his own experience posted to a rural hospital in 1916–18. They were published piecemeal in medical journals and elsewhere between 1925 and 1927, and the dry, medical-record-like prose here is the starting point of his narrative tone.

title: The White Guard
significance: A novel that watches, from inside one family's home, a winter of repeated changes of regime in Kyiv in 1918. It began serialization in 1925 in the magazine Russia but was cut off, and the complete edition appeared later abroad.

title: The Days of the Turbins
significance: A play adapting The White Guard for the stage of the Moscow Art Theatre. Though attacked for portraying White Army officers as human beings, its run continued, and it was almost the only success that stayed on stage during his lifetime.

title: The Master and Margarita
significance: A novel he revised from 1928 until his death, in which the devil's retinue's visit to Moscow crosses with Pontius Pilate's Jerusalem. It is a posthumous publication, serialized in censored form in the magazine Moskva in November 1966 and January 1967, and the uncut edition did not appear in the Soviet Union until 1973.

title: Heart of a Dog
significance: A novella satirizing the making of a new human being through an experiment that transplants human organs into a stray dog. He wrote it in 1925 but publication was blocked; the first Russian edition appeared abroad in 1968, a posthumous publication, and it was not published within the Soviet Union until 1987.

title: The Story of My Dovecote
significance: A story about a boy who has passed his gymnasium entrance exam and encounters a pogrom on the day he goes to buy pigeons. It was published in 1925 in the magazine Red Virgin Soil and is the starting point of his childhood story cycle.

title: Red Cavalry
significance: A cycle recording his experience serving in the 1920 Polish-Soviet War in some thirty short stories. It provoked public objection from Red Cavalry commander Budyonny, and it became an example of writing the revolution's war without heroic narrative.

title: Sunset
significance: A play about a son pushing his father aside within a Jewish transport-business family in Odessa. It premiered in Baku in 1927 and was staged the following year at the Moscow Art Theatre, but it was soon dropped from the repertoire.

title: Odessa Tales
significance: A cycle set in Odessa's Moldavanka district, centered on the gang boss Benya Krik. Stories published separately through the 1920s were gathered into a single volume in 1931.

title: Gypsy Ballads
significance: A cycle of eighteen ballads on the subject of the Gypsies of Andalusia. By setting avant-garde metaphor over the eight-syllable meter of the oral ballad, it made him the most widely read poet in Spain.

title: Blood Wedding
significance: A tragedy that begins when a bride flees with a former lover on her wedding day. It started from a real-life incident, and in the second half the Moon and Death appear as characters, turning the prose stage into poetry.

title: Yerma
significance: The process by which a childless rural woman is driven to catastrophe within the discipline of honor and gossip. Among the late trilogy, it gives the greatest weight to chorus and ritual scenes.

title: Poet in New York
significance: Poems written during his 1929–30 stay in New York, which abandon folk meter to treat the imagery of the Depression-era city through surrealist juxtaposition. It was not published until 1940, after the poet's death.

title: The House of Bernarda Alba
significance: A tragedy that begins with a mother in mourning confining her five daughters to the house under an eight-year discipline of grief. He finished it in June 1936, and its premiere took place posthumously in Buenos Aires in 1945.
